subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Sen no Rikyu: The Tea Master
description: A fast breakdown of Sen no Rikyu: The Tea Master for builders.

hook.text: Sen no Rikyu transformed tea ceremony from an elite display of wealth into a practice of humble simplicity.

buildup.text: In the 16th century, he served Japan's most powerful warlord, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, as his personal tea master.

discovery.text: Rikyu replaced gold tea rooms with tiny rustic huts. He valued rough pottery over Chinese porcelain. Less was more.

twist.text: Hideyoshi ordered Rikyu to commit ritual suicide (seppuku) in 1591. The exact reason remains one of Japanese history's mysteries.

climax.text: Rikyu's aesthetic—wabi tea—became the dominant philosophy. His influence on Japanese culture remains unmatched centuries later.

punchline.text: Simplicity over gold, humility over power. One tea master changed a nation.

quiz.question: What was Sen no Rikyu's most important contribution to tea ceremony?
options: He replaced luxury with rustic simplicity (wabi tea)
He built the largest tea house

details.summary: Sen no Rikyu (1522-1591) is the most influential figure in Japanese tea history. He transformed the tea ceremony from an ostentatious display of wealth into a practice of radical simplicity. His principles of harmony, respect, purity, and tranquility define the tea ceremony to this day.
details.whyItMatters: Rikyu's vision of beauty in simplicity influenced not just tea but all of Japanese aesthetics. His tragic death added a layer of legend to his already towering legacy.
takeaways: Sen no Rikyu is the most influential figure in Japanese tea
He transformed the ceremony into one of radical simplicity
He was ordered to commit ritual suicide in 1591

faq.question: Why was Sen no Rikyu ordered to commit suicide?
faq.answer: The exact reason remains debated. His patron, warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi, may have been offended by Rikyu's independence, political influence, or refusal to compromise his aesthetic principles. Some theories involve a dispute over a gate statue. Rikyu performed seppuku in 1591 at age 69.

faq.question: What did Sen no Rikyu change about the tea ceremony?
faq.answer: He rejected expensive Chinese ceramics in favor of humble Korean and Japanese pottery. He shrank the tea room to a tiny hut. He chose simple seasonal flowers over elaborate arrangements. He made tea an act of spiritual humility rather than a display of wealth and power.
